correctness.rationale: The degree-four and degree-five Gegenbauer factorizations reduce the largest-zero trajectories to explicit products A_n B_{n,d}. Standard complete-Bernstein closure properties prove membership up to d=3 and d=4, while the reversed Pick orientation of B_{n,d} on a real interval excludes every larger d. Stieltjes inversion gives the endpoint densities. Symbolic checks reproduce the polynomial and zero formulas, and high-precision quadrature reproduces both endpoint integral representations.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant source arXiv:2609.19186 gives a nonoptimal sufficient largest-zero range for n>=4, explicitly separates the exact n=2,3 cases, and does not state the degree-four and degree-five exact thresholds or the compact endpoint measures. Targeted searches by source identifier, exact low-degree formulas, largest Gegenbauer/ultraspherical zeros, complete Bernstein/Pick terminology, and endpoint scales found no equivalent statement. Residual risk remains because the source is recent and equivalent elementary low-degree observations could use different terminology.

value.rationale: The theorem closes the first two unresolved largest-zero threshold cases, strictly improves the known sufficient endpoint in each, and identifies the sharp analytic mechanism. The endpoint Stieltjes measures add an explicit structural description beyond membership alone.
